the Convention on the rights of the child (CRC) in Argentina has had a significant impact on domestic politics, but the impact of the Convention is not the same across all areas of children’s rights.

The main takeaway from our work is that
domestic advocacy coalitions are the key mechanism by which global rights conventions promote domestic compliance.
the global normative context is not a static backdrop against which politics unfolds but rather an active force in the construction of domestic political opportunities.
the domestic impact of global norms depends on the ability of domestic actors to translate these norms into domestic political opportunities.
